newsitem.title: USA: USAir to buy 120 Airbus aircraft.
newsitem.headline: USAir to buy 120 Airbus aircraft.

text.p: USAir Group Inc. said Wednesday it agreed to buy 120 Airbus Industrie aircraft in a deal that could be worth more than $5 billion and took an option to buy as many as 280 additional planes.

The order is a major victory for Airbus, the European consortium, and a blow to Boeing Co., the world's largest aircraft manufacturer, and McDonnell Douglas Corp., whose commercial aircraft business has struggled.
The deal, which will allow USAir to streamline its fleet and reduce costs, includes orders for single-aisle Airbus A319, A320 and A321 models, the airline said.
It gave no indication of the value of the order.
But industry sources put the total cost at $5.3 billion, based on list prices for the aircraft. Airlines often get discounts depending on their orders and relationship with the manufacturer.
Because all three aircraft have the same cockpit, systems and common engine types, USAir said the deal will help cut its operating costs for crew training, scheduling and maintenance.

If the Herndon, Va.-based airline exercises options for all the additional aircraft, the order could be worth as much as $12 billion based on list prices, according to the Wall Street Journal, which reported the deal in Wednesday editions.
It quoted people familiar with the purchase agreement as saying the airline had won "aggressive" discounts.

In a statement, USAir said the deal was part of its bid to reduce aircraft and engine types. It noted that the A320 series will replace many of the DC-9-30s, B-737-200s, F-28s and MD-80s currently in its fleet.
The four different aircraft with three different engine types will be replaced by a single aircraft family with one engine type.

"The market in the eastern U.S. is moving to a lower-fare environment that brings with it increased demand. These aircraft, and the flexibility we have in executing orders among aircraft types, will give us cost-efficient planes of the right size," USAir Chairman Stephen Wolf said in a statement.
In addition to the firm orders, USAir took options for 120 more aircraft with set delivery dates and 160 other planes.

USAir said it would enter talks with engine manufacturers for the engines to power the new aircraft and also would begin examining alternatives for wide-body aircraft to support its growing international operations.

All three aircraft models feature flight controls meant to reduce pilot workload, protect against windshear, stalling or overspeeding, reduce mechanical complexity and improve smoothness and stability, USAir said.

The Airbus A319 is a twin-engine 122-seat aircraft with a range of 3,000 nautical miles, the A320 a twin-engine 144-seat aircraft with a range of 2,900 nautical miles and the A321 a twin-engine 168-seat aircraft with a range of 2,700 miles.
USAir will configure its new aircraft with 12 seats in first class for the A319 and A320 and 24 for the A321, with the balance in coach.
USAir stock gained 75 cents to $18.875 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
